findings.title: First-use inserts can commit without the required owner effects
findings.details: lock_daily_head(create_first=True) directly inserts S38 and lock_execution(create_first=True) directly inserts S44 before idempotent_outcome. Their exact first-head revision-one and first-session START completion checks exist only in RestrictedSqlSession.validate_completion, which is invoked only after idempotent_outcome's mutation callback. execute_command calls operation(transaction), then finish(), then commits. finish checks only registry acquisition, S01 and exact leased artifact identities. A correctly guarded internal CommitBundle callback can stop immediately after first-head creation, leaving ACTIVE S38 revision zero/null bundle with no S39-S42/S27 success/S29 COMMITTED/S02-S04. A correctly guarded StartSession callback can stop after first-session creation, leaving READY S44 with no current P/A eligibility, S45 or S02-S04. The operation does not need raw SQL or a generic insert capability. New first-use writes therefore escape the sole owner's full atomic boundary despite the service happy path completing correctly.

findings.title: Preflight-miss retries can lose an already committed historical result
findings.details: publish, commit and start attempt a receipt-only preflight replay, but after a miss their operation invokes _registry before execution_historical_outcome. Consider an identical retry whose preflight sees no receipt, followed by the original committing, followed by a relevant artifact revoke committing before the retry reaches registry entry. The retry now rejects in the registry guard before it can read the original successful receipt, although the exact historical result exists and must remain replayable with executable=false. Artifact expiry/deletion and START's pre-registry current-bundle join provide additional live-state failures on this path. The under-S01 history read closes only races where current authority remains admissible. The recorded sequential authority-loss replay and same-key first-use contention do not exercise the preflight-miss/original-commit/authority-loss order.

findings.title: Hold/stop cases do not establish canonical active control denial
findings.details: The new hold/stop branches write S18.status=PROTECTIVE_HOLD or STOP and S17.status=PROTECTIVE_HOLD or STOP, then also advance S01 epoch. The unchanged _current_control_states proves an active control only for S18.status=ACTIVE and S17.status in HOLD/STOP/RESTRICTION; these rows are therefore UNKNOWN/unproven control projections. The START failure assertion allows any RepositoryTransactionError and also has a stale epoch, so it cannot demonstrate that canonical active HOLD/STOP is the denying input. Existing KL022 tests use ACTIVE + HOLD/STOP, but the exact KL019 service pass oracle explicitly requires active control cases.
